source.title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals

accepted.question_text: Classify all recurrent one-sided and two-sided sequences over a finite alphabet whose maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n)=2n for every n≥1; equivalently, determine all one-sided and two-sided pattern Sturmian sequences.

evidence.quote: The sequence x is pattern Sturmian if p∗(n) = 2n for all n ≥ 1. Note that a Sturmian sequence is necessarily pattern Sturmian. The converse inclusion, however, does not hold. Problem 2.1.1 Determine all single sided (resp. double sided) sequences that are pattern Sturmian.

accepted.question_text: For the discrete Schrödinger operator H on l²(Z) with potential λx_m generated by a pattern Sturmian sequence x, does the Sturmian conclusion remain valid: is the spectrum σ(H) always a zero-Lebesgue-measure Cantor set and are all spectral measures singular continuous?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.1.1 Let λ ∈ C and let x ∈ {0, 1}^Z be a Sturmian sequence. Denote by H the Schrödinger operator defined in the space l2(Z) ... Then, the spectrum σ (H) of the operator H is a zero Lebesgue measure Cantor set. Furthermore, all spectral measures are singular continuous. ... Conjecture 2.1.1 Theorem 2.1.1 holds if x is a pattern Sturmian sequence.

accepted.question_text: Let (V,E) be the graph of the Penrose tiling and define H on l²(V) by [Hψ](v)=∑_{w:(v,w)∈E}(ψ(w)-ψ(v)). Determine the spectrum σ(H) of this operator.

evidence.quote: Consider for example the Penrose tiling and the corresponding graph (V, E), where V is the vertex set and E the set of edges. Define the operator H in the space l2(V) as follows: for any ψ ∈ l2(V) and any v ∈ V, let [Hψ](v) := ∑_{w :(v,w)∈E}(ψ(w) − ψ(v)). Problem 2.1.2 Determine the spectrum σ (H) of the operator defined above.

accepted.question_text: Consider the Schrödinger operator H on l²(Z²) with potential V(m,n)=s_1^{λ1}(m)+s_2^{λ2}(n), where s_j^{λ_j}(k)=λ_j·χ_[1-γ,1)({kγ}) and γ=(√5−1)/2. Do there exist complex parameters λ1 and λ2 for which the spectrum σ(H) is a Cantorval, meaning that it equals the closure of its interior and has no isolated connected component?

evidence.quote: s_j^{λj}(k) := λj · χ[1−γ ,1)({kγ }) ... V(m, n) := s_1^{λ1}(m) + s_2^{λ2}(n). The corresponding Schrödinger operator H in the space l2(Z2) is defined as follows ... Conjecture 2.1.2 There exist values of λ1 and λ2 such that the spectrum σ (H) of H is a Cantorval; that is, the spectrum is the closure of its interior and no connected component is isolated.

accepted.question_text: Does every one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ have pure point spectrum whenever its abelianisation (substitution) matrix M has irreducible characteristic polynomial, equivalently whenever the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.1 (Pisot substitution conjecture) A one-dimensional self-similar inflation tiling with Pisot scaling factor λ has pure point spectrum if its abelianisation matrix (i.e. its substitution matrix) M has an irreducible characteristic polynomial; that is, if the algebraic degree of λ equals the dimension of M (or the number of tile types).

accepted.question_text: Does every one-dimensional unimodular Pisot inflation tiling have pure point spectrum whenever the first rational Čech cohomology group of its tiling space has rank equal to the algebraic degree of the Pisot scaling factor λ?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.2 (Homological Pisot Conjecture) A one-dimensional, unimodular Pisot inflation tiling has pure point spectrum if its first rational Cech cohomology group has rank equal to the algebraic degree of λ.

accepted.question_text: For a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling with scaling factor λ, must the coincidence rank divide the algebraic norm of λ?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.2.3 (Coincidence Rank Conjecture) The coincidence rank of a one-dimensional Pisot inflation tiling must divide the algebraic norm of λ.

accepted.question_text: For the diffraction measure of a Pinwheel tiling, determine which radii support sharp rings and compute the intensity carried by each such ring.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3.1 Determine the position of sharp rings in the diffraction measure of a Pinwheel Tiling and their intensity.

accepted.question_text: Does the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel tiling have a nonzero absolutely continuous component?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3.2 Does the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel Tiling contain an absolutely continuous component?

accepted.question_text: Let α,β∈R be such that 1, α, and β are Q-linearly independent, let Y(α,β) be the canonical cut-and-project set formed from E(α,β)={(x,y,αx+βy):x,y∈R}⊂R³, and for a shape Ω⊂E(α,β) let ξ_(α,β)(Ω) be the set of distinct frequencies of type-2 patches of shape Ω occurring in Y(α,β). Is there a choice of α and β for which sup over all aligned squares Ω of #ξ_(α,β)(Ω) is infinite?

evidence.quote: Let α, β ∈ R be such that 1, α and β are Q-linearly independent. Let Y (α, β) be a canonical cut-and-project set ... Given a shape Ω ⊂ E(α, β), let ξ(α,β)(Ω) denote the set of different frequencies of patches of shape Ω in Y (α, β) ... Problem 2.4.1 Is there a choice of α and β as above such that sup_{Ω∈S} #ξ(α,β)(Ω) = +∞, where S denotes the collection of all aligned squares?

accepted.question_text: With the same cut-and-project setup and notation as in Problem 2.4.1, is there a choice of α and β for which the supremum over all aligned rectangles Ω of the number of distinct frequencies #ξ_(α,β)(Ω) is infinite?

evidence.quote: The following is a seemingly easier version of the previous problem. Problem 2.4.2 Is there a choice of α and β as above such that sup_{Ω∈R} #ξ(α,β)(Ω) = +∞, where R denotes the collection of aligned rectangles?

accepted.question_text: Suppose (α,β)∈R² with 1, α, and β Q-linearly independent satisfies lim inf_{n→∞} n||nα||·||nβ|| = 0, i.e. the Littlewood-conjecture-type condition displayed as equation (3) in the paper. Does this imply the aligned-rectangle frequency divergence condition sup_{Ω∈R} #ξ_(α,β)(Ω)=+∞ from equation (2)?

evidence.quote: Using the arguments in Haynes et al. (2016b, c), it can be shown that any such pair satisfies the equation lim inf_{n→∞} n ||nα|| ||nβ|| = 0; ... Whether the converse holds is an open problem:
Problem 2.4.3 Given (α, β) ∈ R2 such that 1, α and β are Q-linearly independent, does (3) imply (2)?

accepted.question_text: For an aperiodic repetitive tiling of dimension d, does polynomial patch complexity growth p(n)=O(n^d) force the rational Čech cohomology of the tiling space to be finitely generated, i.e. rk(H*(Ω,Q))<∞?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5.1 With the same notation, is it the case that for an aperiodic, repetitive tiling of dimension d, if p(n) = O(nd), then rk(H∗(Ω, Q)) < ∞?

accepted.question_text: Let D⊂R² be a Delone set that is bi-Lipschitz equivalent to Z². Must there exist a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism L:R²→R² such that L(D)=Z²?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.6.1 Let D ⊂ R2 be a Delone set BL to Z2. Does there exist a bi-Lipschitz map L : R2 → R2 such that L(D) = Z2?

accepted.question_text: Identify and classify tilings that possess some strengthened geometric pattern property—motivated by properties such as bounded displacement equivalence, bi-Lipschitz equivalence, linear repetitivity, or similar notions—with the feature that every tiling mutually locally derivable from it, topologically conjugate to it, or homeomorphic to it also has that same property.
accepted.context_brief: Pattern properties invariant under tiling equivalence

evidence.quote: A natural question is thus to ask whether one can reconcile the two approaches. One strategy to answer this question is to consider a strong version of the BD or BL or LR or ... properties. Problem 2.7.1 Classify tilings with such a property that any other tiling MLD (or topologically conjugate, or homeomorphic) to it also has that property.

accepted.question_text: Develop and analyze new geometric properties of tilings, analogous to but not identical with bounded displacement, bi-Lipschitz equivalence, linear repetitivity, and related notions, that are invariant under mutual local derivability, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism of tiling spaces.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.7.2 Develop and study new geometric properties, analogous but not identical to BD, BL, etc., that are invariant under MLD, topological conjugacy, or homeomorphism.

accepted.question_text: Find a set of local matching rules for tilings in dimension 2 or 3 such that both of the following hold: (A) for each tile type t there is a constant c_t with discrepancy D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)·vol(R)| bounded by c_t·|∂R| for every finite union R of tiles, and (B) the same low-fluctuation bound also holds for every pattern or patch satisfying the matching rules.

evidence.quote: (A) ... there exists a constant ct depending only on the tile t such that Dt(R) ≤ ct · |∂R| ... (B) The second condition is that property (A) should also hold for any pattern or patch satisfying the given matching rule. Problem 2.7.3 Find a set of matching rules in dimension 2 and/or 3 that meet both condition (A) and condition (B).

accepted.question_text: Find a set of matching rules for a two-dimensional tiling that satisfies the low-fluctuation condition (A): for every tile type t there is c_t such that D_t(R)=|N_t(R)-d(t)·vol(R)| is at most c_t·|∂R| for every finite union R of tiles.

evidence.quote: The following statement can be seen as a first step to the solution of Problem 2.7.3. Problem 2.7.4 Find a set of matching rules in dimension 2 satisfying condition (A) only.

accepted.question_text: Determine all Borel probability measures on the space Cl(R^d) of closed subsets of R^d that are invariant under the natural action of SL_d(R), and likewise determine all such invariant Borel probability measures for the action of the affine group ASL_d(R).
accepted.context_brief: Invariant measures on closed subsets of Euclidean space

evidence.quote: Let d ≥ 1 be an integer. Denote by Cl(Rd) the set of all closed subsets of Rd with respect to the Chabauty–Fell topology ... Problem 2.8.1 (J. Marklof) Determine all SLd (R)-invariant Borel probability measures on Cl(Rd) and similarly for the ASLd (R) action.

accepted.question_text: Let E⊂R^k be a totally irrational d-dimensional subspace, and let Y be the cut-and-project set obtained from E using a bounded window W with nonempty interior and with boundary ∂W of zero (k−d)-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Must Y always be bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice in E?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.8.2 Let E ⊂ Rk be a totally irrational subspace of dimension d ≥ 1, and let Y be a cut-and-project set obtained from E using a bounded window W with non-empty interior and with the property that the (k − d)-dimensional Lebesgue measure of ∂W is zero. Is such a set Y always BL to a lattice in E?
